item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The effect of 426 is that anyone talking about it will refer to it in the first person - it does not actually change the perception of others. Noticing the effect is relatively easy, but effectively communicating about it is another thing entirely. A conversation noticing the effect might look something like:

  • Alice: What's in that room?
  • Bob: I'm probably some monster, or maybe I'm nothing.
  • Alice: Why did you just refer to me in the first person?
  • Bob: I wasn't talking about you, I was talking about myself in that room.
  • Alice: Did I say me? I was talking about myself!
  • Bob: What?
  • Charlie: Both of you have been talking about me in the first person.
  • Alice and Bob: WHAT?!?

It's likely that containment personnel have to explicitly refer to themselves in the third person, since any first-person reference is ambiguous to 426's effect.

item.content:encoded:
It makes sense, in the era the SCP was written.

D-class underwent monthly terminations. Exceptions were granted in the case of testing protocols or extreme/unusual circumstances.

In this case, the D-class had passed the two-month time it takes for individuals to self-identify as a toaster. As D/426/4 was not apparently affected in any way, there was no real reason to keep him around anymore, and was therefore terminated at the end of the next monthly termination cycle.

item.title: Heritage?
item.content:encoded:
So, I read this SCP, read it again, then read it some more. But of course, that really doesn't matter, it's an upvote from me. Now, on to the actual point;

Is this every going to become a heritage SCP? I mean, it's got the upvotes. It's been here for at least 3 years (well, I believe it has, anyone who wants to tell me when this was first posted can correct me). But of course, it's the original format screw. SCP-●●|●●●●●|●●|●, SCP-732, all the format screws; they're all here because of the original format screw, this bloody toaster. (OK, I'm probably exaggerating it, but my point still stands, this is a heritage SCP if I ever saw one).
